title: Extension by zero of abelian Zariski sheaves is a left adjoint of restriction to an open
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, $U\subseteq X$ an open subscheme, and $X_{\rm Zar}$, $U_{\rm Zar}$ the small Zariski sites of $X$ and of $U$ [def-sc-zariski-site] (the objects of $U_{\rm Zar}$ are the opens $W\subseteq U$, which are also objects of $X_{\rm Zar}$, and a family of opens of $W$ is a covering of $W$ in $U_{\rm Zar}$ if and only if it is one in $X_{\rm Zar}$). Let $\textit{Ab}(X_{\rm Zar})$, $\textit{Ab}(U_{\rm Zar})$ be the abelian categories of abelian sheaves on these sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. For $\mathcal G\in\textit{Ab}(X_{\rm Zar})$ let $\mathcal G|_U\in\textit{Ab}(U_{\rm Zar})$ be the abelian sheaf $W\mapsto\mathcal G(W)$ ($W\subseteq U$ open) with the restriction maps of $\mathcal G$, and for a morphism $\psi$ of $\textit{Ab}(X_{\rm Zar})$ let $(\psi|_U)_W=\psi_W$. For $\mathcal F\in\textit{Ab}(U_{\rm Zar})$ let $j_{p!}\mathcal F$ be the presheaf of abelian groups on $X_{\rm Zar}$ with $(j_{p!}\mathcal F)(V)=\mathcal F(V)$ if $V\subseteq U$ and $(j_{p!}\mathcal F)(V)=0$ if $V\not\subseteq U$ ($V\subseteq X$ open), whose restriction map along $V'\subseteq V$ is the restriction map of $\mathcal F$ if $V\subseteq U$ (then also $V'\subseteq U$) and $0$ otherwise; a morphism $\alpha:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F'$ of $\textit{Ab}(U_{\rm Zar})$ gives $j_{p!}\alpha$, equal to $\alpha_V$ for $V\subseteq U$ and to $0$ otherwise. Let $\theta_{\mathcal F}:j_{p!}\mathcal F\to j_!\mathcal F$ be the sheafification of $j_{p!}\mathcal F$ as a presheaf of abelian groups on the site $X_{\rm Zar}$ [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], and $j_!\alpha:j_!\mathcal F\to j_!\mathcal F'$ the unique morphism with $j_!\alpha\circ\theta_{\mathcal F}=\theta_{\mathcal F'}\circ j_{p!}\alpha$; $j_!\mathcal F$ is the *extension of $\mathcal F$ by zero*. Then: (1) $\mathcal F\mapsto j_!\mathcal F$, $\alpha\mapsto j_!\alpha$ is an additive functor $j_!:\textit{Ab}(U_{\rm Zar})\to\textit{Ab}(X_{\rm Zar})$; (2) $j_!$ is left adjoint to restriction: for every $\mathcal F\in\textit{Ab}(U_{\rm Zar})$ and every $\mathcal G\in\textit{Ab}(X_{\rm Zar})$ the map $\Hom_{\textit{Ab}(X_{\rm Zar})}(j_!\mathcal F,\mathcal G)\to\Hom_{\textit{Ab}(U_{\rm Zar})}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G|_U)$, $\psi\mapsto(\psi\circ\theta_{\mathcal F})|_U$ (whose component at $W\subseteq U$ is $\psi_W\circ\theta_{\mathcal F,W}:\mathcal F(W)\to\mathcal G(W)$), is bijective, and natural in $\mathcal F$ and in $\mathcal G$.

proof.text: Step 1 (restriction). Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ and let $e:(\operatorname{Opens}U)^{op}\to(\operatorname{Opens}X)^{op}$ send an open to its image. Restriction is precomposition with $e$ on underlying presheaves, restricted to sheaves [def-sc-zariski-site, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Mathlib Topology.IsOpenEmbedding.sheafPullback gives this functor R, and sheafPullbackIso identifies the usual TopCat.Sheaf.pullback with R.

proof.text: Step 2 (the presheaf). Construct $E=\mathrm{forget}_U\circ\operatorname{Lan}_e$ using Mathlib Functor.lan, and put $P(F)=E(F)$. This is an actual colimit construction. The functor e is fully faithful, since inclusion of U is injective. The pointwise Kan-extension unit is therefore an isomorphism (LeftExtension.IsPointwiseLeftKanExtension.isIso_hom). If $V\subseteq U$, the image of $j^{-1}V$ equals V (Opens.functor_map_eq_inf), so mapping this equality and inverting the unit gives $P(F)(V)\cong F(j^{-1}V)$. If $V\not\subseteq U$, an object of CostructuredArrow e (op V) would give $V\subseteq j(W)\subseteq U$, a contradiction. Thus the indexing diagram is zero, vacuously, and IsColimit.isZero_pt gives $P(F)(V)=0$. These arguments include V empty, U empty, and U=X.

proof.text: Step 3 (sheafification). Set $L=E\circ\mathrm{presheafToSheaf}$ and $\theta_F=\mathrm{toSheafify}(P(F))$ [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. For every sheaf H and presheaf morphism $\eta:P(F)\to H$, apply the inverse of sheafificationAdjunction.homEquiv to obtain the factorization. The equivalence apply_symm_apply proves its defining equation, and injectivity of the equivalence proves uniqueness.

proof.text: Step 4 (adjunction). Compose Functor.lanAdjunction for e with sheafificationAdjunction [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Restrict this composite along fullyFaithfulSheafToPresheaf on U and the identity on sheaves on X, using Adjunction.restrictFullyFaithful. The two comparison isomorphisms are reflexivity: restriction of underlying presheaves is the underlying presheaf of R. This gives $L\dashv R$. Transport the right adjoint by the inverse of sheafPullbackIso to obtain $L\dashv j^{-1}$. Its hom equivalences are bijective by Equiv.bijective. The composite adjunction is exactly composition with theta followed by the Kan hom equivalence, so it realizes the map in the statement.

proof.text: Step 5 (additivity). Give L its IsLeftAdjoint instance using the adjunction of Step 4. It preserves binary coproducts and zero morphisms. In preadditive sheaf categories, preservesBinaryBiproducts_of_preservesBinaryCoproducts turns this into preservation of binary biproducts, and Functor.additive_of_preservesBinaryBiproducts yields Functor.Additive L. Together with Steps 2 and 3 and the adjunction of Step 4 this proves all clauses.
